hints: LCA in a BST needs no recursion into both sides: while a and b are both on the same side of root, move to that side. The first node where they split is the LCA.
floor: every time you step RIGHT, the node you leave is <= x - a candidate. Remember the latest candidate; it is the answer when you fall off the tree.
printRange prunes: only descend left when root->key > lo, and right when root->key < hi. Without pruning it is still correct, just O(n).
source: Standard BST questions (the ordering lets each walk ONE path)
title: BST queries: LCA, floor, ceil, range
